hypotheses.statement: Management view (CRO): growth slowed because a new competitor is undercutting us on price
hypotheses.implication: Price pressure exists at the margin (price cited in 34% of lost deals, average deal size down from €53.7k to €49.7k), but new-logo ARR still grew and only 31% of churned customers cite a competitor or price; the slowdown is not a win-the-deal problem
hypotheses.rationale: Rejected as the explanation of the slowdown: new-logo ARR rose €0.2M and win rate held at 23% to 24%, while churn rose €4.5M

hypotheses.statement: Growth slowed because churned ARR surged, not because acquisition fell
hypotheses.implication: The 2026 budget must address retention first; adding acquisition into a leaking base buys less ARR

hypotheses.statement: The February 2025 onboarding cut drove the first-year churn spike (customers never reach value)
hypotheses.implication: Reversing the €0.8M saving is the cheapest lever on the biggest leak
hypotheses.rationale: Timing, mechanism (time to first value 21 to 48 days) and exit interviews (58% never fully implemented) line up; mature customers also churn 9%, so onboarding is not the whole story, and causality is not proven by a controlled test

hypotheses.statement: Sales capacity is the binding constraint on growth (not enough account executives)
hypotheses.implication: No source shows deals lost for lack of sellers; pipeline grew 18% and deals won rose from 175 to 193 with the current team. Hiring should be phased and gated until capacity is shown to bind

hypotheses.statement: The 30-AE plan will add €9M of new ARR in 2026
hypotheses.implication: With a 9-month ramp, 30 AEs hired in Q1 deliver at most about €4.5M in 2026, half the promise, for €3.6M a year
hypotheses.rationale: €9M equals 30 AEs at full productivity for a full year; the 9-month ramp makes that impossible in 2026

hypotheses.statement: The expansion decline has the same root cause as first-year churn (customers who never implemented do not expand)
hypotheses.implication: Expansion recovery is counted as an upper-bound lever to be validated, not a certainty
